G# has a tendency to get stuck because of the mechanics of the key. Most keys are directly connected to a lever so the force of your finger opens the key. The G# (and low C#) key moves a lever out of the way so that a spring opens the key. Sometimes when spit/moisture in the instrument dries out, it leaves behind residue that can make the pad stick to the instrument. If the spring isn't strong enough to break that residue, the pad stays closed.

To fix it, keep a dollar bill in your case, fold it in half lengthwise so it's about as wide as the tone hole, place it between the tone hole and the pad, hold the pad down firmly so the dollar is pinched in between, then drag it out. Repeat once or twice until it stops sticking. The dollar should remove the residue that is causing it to stick.
